enquiry: We produce a clear, colourless aqueous sucrose solution and want to monitor its sucrose concentration in-line. The solution flows through a 50 mm stainless steel pipe at 20 to 30 °C and normal pressure; the expected range is 5 to 15 % w/w and our quality limit is plus or minus 0.3 % w/w. Our laboratory refractometer is the reference method and stays in use. The analyser can stand in a dry, safe room 10 m from the pipe, and the line is cleaned in place with hot caustic once a day. A reading every minute is enough. Please propose a method and probe for a first trial.

proposal.next_step: Run the single-method feasibility trial of the NIR transflection/transmission probe with Raman as comparison, calibrated against the refractometer across 5-15 % w/w and 20-30 °C.

assessment.chemometrics_note: A PLS calibration against the refractometer reference is needed because NIR bands overlap; it should span 5-15 % w/w and the 20-30 °C temperature range, and be validated on held-out samples before judging the plus or minus 0.3 % w/w limit.
assessment.realtime_tracking_note: A reading every minute is compatible with fiber-probe NIR acquisition; the sources note online measurements require high-speed spectral acquisition and that diode-array analyzers record all wavelengths simultaneously, which suits fast monitoring.
assessment.future_direction: If the trial shows the single NIR model meets the limit, a later step could evaluate a compact LED-based NIR sensor at the pipe for a lower-cost permanent installation.

proposal.what_would_change_it: If other dissolved solids are present (Q1), the calibration design and the refractometer reference both need rethinking; if no CIP-rated fitting exists or the analyzer must stay 10 m away and the NIR trial misses the accuracy limit, the Raman comparison or a near-pipe MIR-ATR variant becomes relevant.
proposal.next_step: Run the single-method feasibility trial of the NIR transflection/transmission probe with Raman as comparison, calibrated against the refractometer across 5-15 % w/w and 20-30 °C.

assessment.brief_answer: For a first trial, we recommend an NIR transmission or transflection probe in the 50 mm pipe, calibrated against your laboratory refractometer across 5 to 15 % w/w sucrose, with a Raman probe as a comparison. Key open items are whether any other dissolved solids are present, the pipe fitting and its CIP rating, and whether your quality limit of plus or minus 0.3 % w/w is achieved.
